meta.title: Mossbank Growers — Pollinator survey 2025–2026
meta.description: Research readout for the Mossbank Growers Cooperative members' assembly: a two-season wild bee survey on 30 orchard farms shows that farms with 2 km of new hedgerow count 2.1× more wild bees and harvest 9% more fruit, and asks members to co-fund hedgerows on 40 more farms.

slides.eyebrow: Mossbank Growers Cooperative · Pollinator survey 2025–2026 · Members' assembly · 4 December
slides.heading: New hedgerows doubled our wild bees and lifted yields 9%.
slides.lead: 30 member farms, two seasons, 1,440 bee walks.
slides.notes: Lead with the answer. Members who stop after slide 2 still know what we found and what we ask.

slides.heading: Three findings make the case for hedgerow on more member farms

cards.title: More wild bees
cards.body: Hedgerow farms counted 2.1× more wild bees per walk: 46 against 22.

cards.title: More fruit
cards.body: Apple yield ran 9% higher: 31.6 t/ha against 29.0 t/ha.

cards.title: Whole orchard
cards.body: The gain reached the centre rows, 400 m from the nearest hedge.

slides.heading: We asked whether 2 km of hedgerow pays its way on an orchard
slides.lead: Rented hives cost members €310 per hectare each spring. Wild bees are free, if they have a place to nest.

slides.heading: We walked 1,440 bee counts on 30 farms over two seasons

stats.label: 14 planted ≥2 km of hedgerow in 2023–24; 16 did not

slides.heading: Three findings
slides.lead: Bees, fruit, and which bees came back.

slides.heading: Hedgerow farms counted about twice the wild bees in both seasons
slides.lead: Wild bees per 100 m walk, mean; 14 hedgerow farms, 16 without. Source: cooperative survey, n = 1,440 walks.
slides.notes: The gap grew from 1.95× in 2025 to 2.2× in 2026 as the hedges filled out. That is the point to stress: the effect is still rising.

slides.quote: I used to rent 40 hives for bloom. Last April the hedge was humming before the hives arrived.
slides.by: Farm 11 · apple grower, 18 ha · planted 2.3 km of hedgerow in 2023

slides.heading: Apple yield ran 9% higher on hedgerow farms, worth €1,170 per hectare
Ground-nesting mining bees made up more than half of the gain
slides.lead: Extra wild bees per 100 m walk on hedgerow farms, by group. Total gain: 24 bees per walk.

slides.heading: What it means
slides.lead: One surprise, the limits, and three actions.

slides.heading: We expected an edge effect; the gain reached the orchard centre
slides.left:
Bees stay within 200 m of a hedge
Only the edge rows gain
Centre rows still need hives
slides.right:
Centre rows counted 1.8× more wild bees
Yield rose 7% even 400 m from a hedge
The whole orchard gains

slides.heading: The bee count is solid; the yield link is likely but not proven
rows: Farms chose to plant; not random
Apple prices swing year to year
slides.notes: Say the weak point before members do: farms picked themselves. The 2028 resurvey on newly planted farms is how we test it.

slides.heading: Co-funding hedgerows on 40 more farms ranks first of three actions
slides.lead: Expected yearly gain per farm, ranked. Hedgerow costs €18,000 per 2 km; the cooperative pays half.

items.label: Co-fund 2 km of hedgerow on 40 farms (€360k)
Leave 3 m uncut margins beside hedges (€40k)

slides.heading: Hedgerows bring back the bees: co-fund 40 more farms this winter
slides.lead: €9,000 per farm, €360k in all. A vote today lets members plant before the season closes in March.
